Deflected the Standard Chartered and Prudential-stake questions to the counterparties appropriately. non-obvious takeaways:
- **"No margin fixation" is the key framing** — the 26.7% VNB margin is an OUTPUT of the protection mix, not a target; if savings/non-par recovers, mix normalises and margin could ease WITHOUT signalling deterioration (absolute VNB is the real KPI).

- **Standard Chartered risk is real but capped** — the <5%-single-distributor design means even a StanChart migration is survivable; the ~20%-CAGR partnership-distribution engine is the structural offset.
- **GST/ITC is a self-liquidating drag** — one more quarter then in-base; the "clean" margin/cost run-rate emerges Q3FY27.

deepdive.thesis: A high-quality, protection-led quarter: VNB +24.9% YoY to ₹5.71bn with VNB margin 26.7% (+200bps vs FY26's 24.7%), PAT +27.8% to ₹3.86bn — driven by a deliberate mix-shift toward protection (retail protection APE +60.4% YoY, third straight quarter >40%; total sum assured +31.8% to ₹4.90tn) even as savings softened (non-par squeezed by high FD "sticker prices"). Management explicitly runs to ABSOLUTE VNB GROWTH, not a margin target ("no margin fixation"), and gives NO numeric guidance. Distribution is the moat — 52 banks + 1,500+ partnerships, no single distributor (ex-ICICI Bank ~15%) above 5%; agency turned positive (+2%) and partnership distribution +29.5% (~20% 5-yr CAGR). Overhangs to track: a one-more-quarter GST/ITC-unavailability cost drag (in base from Q3), the Standard Chartered banca relationship amid Prudential's Bharti-AXA promoter move, and a 25th-month persistency dip (81%→77%).
